coauthors.name: Pak-Hang Wong
coauthors.affiliation: Hong Kong Baptist University, Kowloon Tong, Hong Kong
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Philosopher of technology whose core work is literally on cultural values and AI: 'Cultural Differences as Excuses? Human Rights and Cultural Values in Global Ethics and Governance of AI' (Philosophy & Technology 33(4):705-715, 2020) argues that 'cultural differences pose a serious challenge to the ethics and governance of artificial intelligence from a global perspective... malignant actors [may] disregard the demand of important ethical values... by affirming the local culture lacks specific ethical values, e.g., privacy, or by asserting the local culture upholds conflicting values'. Directly about cross-cultural value conflict and value localization in AI.

coauthors.name: Tom Suhr
coauthors.relevance_evidence: First author of 'Challenging the Validity of Personality Tests for Large Language Models' (arXiv:2311.05297): 'it has become popular to attempt to evaluate personality traits of LLMs using questionnaires originally developed for humans... we provide evidence that LLMs' responses to personality tests systematically deviate from human responses, implying that the results of these tests cannot be interpreted in the same way.' This is exactly the construct-validity question underlying value-survey studies (Hofstede/WVS-style questionnaires) applied to LLMs.

coauthors.name: Fariba Karimi
coauthors.affiliation: Complexity Science Hub Vienna, Austria; Graz University of Technology, Austria
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Co-author of 'Linguistic neighbourhoods: explaining cultural borders on Wikipedia through multilingual co-editing activity' (arXiv:1603.04225), which extracts 'significant cultural borders from editing activity of Wikipedia users' across language communities and shows 'how culture is reflected in the collective process of archiving knowledge'; explanatory factors are bilingualism, linguistic similarity and shared religion. Cross-cultural analysis over multilingual text corpora, and she now audits LLM outputs ('Whose Name Comes Up? Auditing LLM-Based Scholar Recommendations').

coauthors.name: Francesco Bonchi
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Co-author of 'Cultures in Community Question Answering' (arXiv:1508.05044): 'We investigate the influence of national culture on people's online questioning and answering behavior... We measure empirically a set of cultural metrics defined in Geert Hofstede's cultural dimensions and Robert Levine's Pace of Life and show that behavioral cultural differences exist in community question answering platforms' across 67 countries. Cross-cultural (Hofstede-dimension) analysis of a natural-language QA platform.

coauthors.name: Carlos Castillo
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Fair ranking, disparate exposure, LLM jailbreaks and 'Discriminatory Compliance: How LLMs Answer Queries from Protected Groups' - demographic/protected-group bias in LLMs, no cultural-values or cross-cultural dimension.

coauthors.name: Ricardo Baeza-Yates
coauthors.affiliation: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm, Sweden; Universitat Pompeu Fabra, Barcelona, Spain

coauthors.name: Sara Hajian
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Discrimination-aware data mining and fair ranking only; no culture/values work in LLMs or NLP found on arXiv.

coauthors.name: Mohamed Megahed
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Student co-author on the FA*IR fair-ranking algorithm only; no cultural-values or LLM work found.
